claims.text: THE NAMED LOCAL NEGATIVE. Norio Hayakawa, who has worked the Dulce question since 1988 and is a proponent of investigating the subject rather than a professional debunker, states on his own site: 'it does not seem to exist'.

Lear heard of Dulce from a woman named as 'Ann West' and developed his Dulce hypothesis in 1988, in the dated chronology of the cluster's originators. The same name appears in Tal Levesque's November 2015 confession as the raw material from which he composed the two original Dulce Base articles.

THE DATED CHRONOLOGY OF THE CLUSTER'S ORIGINATORS. Bennewitz from about 1979; Myrna Hansen's 1980 claim, which Bennewitz later connected to Dulce; Tom Adams in the early 1980s through cattle-mutilation work around 1981; John Lear in 1988, who heard of Dulce from 'Ann West'; and Phil Schneider, not part of the initial rumours, emerging only in 1995.
Hayakawa's own stated conclusion about the alleged Dulce facility, on his own site: 'it does not seem to exist'. He has worked the question since 1988.

Bennewitz is the origin point of the Dulce claim, from about 1979, in the dated chronology of the cluster's originators. Myrna Hansen's 1980 abduction claim was connected to Dulce by Bennewitz after he had begun to suspect a facility there.

Schneider was not part of the initial Dulce rumours and emerged only in 1995, according to Norio Hayakawa's dated chronology of the cluster's originators, which places the initial rumours between about 1979 and the early 1980s.

A further negative exists and is recorded here only so that it is not later mistaken for a check. Norio Hayakawa wrote on 29 August 2016 that an 'alleged' retired Air Force colonel told him no Thomas Edwin Castello was ever employed as security personnel at Dulce. The source is anonymous and Hayakawa brackets him in his own quotation marks.
